title: Mother Russia by Lauren Yee at Signature Theatre #motherrussia #laure...
transcript: I don't know what I was expecting from a play called Mother Russia, but it certainly wasn't what I ended up seeing. This new play by Lauren Yee is about three young adults in St Petersburg, all somewhat drifting in the wake of communism's fall. Part political satire and part spy drama, this is a richly layered critique of capitalism and the fallacy of freedom. I think it's best to leave the plot vague, but do prepare yourself for some offbeat humor and a group of characters who are all oddballs. In addition to the comedy, I was especially impressed by the ways this play frames its ideas. The central plot is captivating on its own, but the mysterious outside fourth character is what ties everything together. What I appreciated the most though is how the setting and these specific characters feel just distant enough, allowing the piece to be thematically resonant without cannibalizing the comedy by hitting too close to home. This was the first piece I’ve seen by Lauren Yee and I was super impressed — at least based on this piece, her voice as a playwright feels so distinct and weird but in a good way. My only criticism here is that Steven Boyer is nowhere near portraying a 25-year-old convincingly. But for how well the actors mesh together, I won't dwell on it. With that, another program for my collection.
